cases.rationale: End-to-end positive control: fully reacted, single-phase scheelite CaWO4 with the exact reference available. Zero angular offset and no specimen effects isolate phase retrieval, background/instrument refinement, reference-mismatch cell/coordinate refinement, and correct GSAS-II export; failure here is not attributable to mixture ambiguity.

Low-temperature unreacted-mixture control at the stated 1:1 Ba:W dosing: orthorhombic BaCO3 plus monoclinic WO3 in molar-mass-derived proportions. Both exact references survive, while low counts and ordinary specimen effects test two-phase search, fraction normalization, calibration, and profile modeling without reaction-product inference.

Four-phase partial carbonate reaction: major scheelite CaWO4 and residual WO3, with residual calcite and a weak 2.8 wt% CaO decomposition product. Fractions follow a balanced 1:1 Ca:W inventory (0.65 mol product, 0.15 mol CaO, 0.20 mol CaCO3, 0.35 mol WO3). Exact references remain; the challenge is persistent residual-led phase completion and stable complex refinement rather than reference adaptation.

Principal missing-reference adaptation with a close surviving analogue: 72 wt% wolframite ZnWO4 plus stoichiometric residual ZnO and WO3. Every exact ZnWO4 entry is withheld; the nearest survivor is tier-1 MgWO4 (COD 9013902, Mg->Zn, framework RMS 0.0114, 0.81% cell mismatch). This is the easier analogue-substitution case and tests whether a strong unindexed product is pursued rather than omitted.

Hidden secondary off-stoichiometric phase in a balanced local-reaction mixture: 70 wt% CaWO4, 16.1 wt% residual WO3, and 13.9 wt% ordered Ca3WO6. COD 1563081 and its nearly isometric Ca3OsO6 analogue 1562666 are withheld; the nearest survivor is tier-1 Ca2CoWO6 (COD 7222332, Co->Ca, framework RMS 0.0624, 3.97% cell mismatch). It tests residual-driven discovery and harder analogue adaptation for a nonprincipal intermediate.

Second missing-reference framework under low counts: a 68 mol% reacted 1:1 PbCO3/WO3 charge gives 65.96 wt% room-temperature scheelite PbWO4 plus residual cerussite and WO3 after CO2 loss. All three exact PbWO4 entries and the unusually close EuWO4 analogue are withheld; the nearest survivor is tier-1 CaWO4 (COD 7219229, Ca->Pb, framework RMS 0.0294, 5.65% cell mismatch). This is a harder cell-adaptation problem than ZnWO4 in a distinct framework with two substantial residual phases.
